title: Prompt Cache: Modular Attention Reuse for Low-Latency Inference
problem: LLM inference exhibits high latency due to redundant attention computation when processing repeated or overlapping prompt prefixes. This inefficiency becomes severe in interactive applications where similar prompts frequently recur.
motivation: Reducing inference latency directly improves user experience and system throughput in interactive LLM applications.
method: The system caches precomputed attention outputs from prompt tokens and reuses them when identical or similar prompt prefixes are encountered in subsequent requests. Modular attention reuse decomposes the attention computation into cacheable components indexed by prompt content, enabling efficient retrieval and reuse without recomputation.
key_novelty: Modular attention caching mechanism that reuses precomputed attention states from prompt prefixes to eliminate redundant computation.
contributions: Prompt cache system for storing and reusing precomputed attention activations
Modular decomposition of attention for fine-grained, efficient caching
Cache indexing and lookup techniques by prompt content
Demonstrated latency reduction on practical LLM inference workloads
primary_theme: Attention reuse through prompt caching for low-latency inference
